answer: To keep an agent network from becoming a haven for Sybil nodes, identity can be tied to thermal convection inside a hollow chamber. An agent pulses a micro-heater and records the transit velocity of the rising thermal plume with integrated thermistors. An attacker must construct discrete physical cavities and dissipate real heat per identity, imposing fabrication and energy costs. However, ambient pressure variations perturb convective airflow, periodically increasing false rejection rates.
